nodes.title: README · Infinite Movie
widgets_values:
# Infinite Movie

Turns a few stills into one seamless, looping film. The MiniMax H3 engine renders one shot per transition between two images; *Cut* joins the chosen shots into the final film; *Even Motion* (optional) smooths camera moves.

Node pack: https://github.com/metamountain/comfyui-infinite-movie (by metamountain). Feedback and issues welcome.

## How to read this workflow
Left: this README (no group). Top: **0 · Engine** (MiniMax H3). Below it ONE row, read left to right – each area has its help note on top:
- **1 · Settings** – LLM (one dropdown), size, output folder, film name.
- **2 · Images** – load your stills (add more: they grow downwards).
- **3 · Prompts** – *Prompt Style* (what the LLM is told, max words, camera) on top, then one *Auto Prompt* per transition.
- **4 · Director** – seconds per shot, loop, variants. Click **AUTO LAYOUT** after changes.
- **5 · Cut** – check the shots, pick A or B, **RENDER VIDEO ▶** makes the film (with sound).
- **6 · Even Motion + Film** – shows the finished film, *Open folder*; Even Motion (off by default) for smooth camera moves.
- **7 · Upscale** (optional, Ctrl+M) – sharper, larger film with RelayVSR x4.
- **8 · Movie to GIF** (optional, Ctrl+M) – a GIF / WebP / MP4 loop of the film.

The settings are passed along one chain: Settings → Prompt Style → Auto Prompts → Director; from there the `sync` link carries them on to Cut → Even Motion.
Before a render starts, Run frees the GPU (unloads the LLM); if it cannot, the render is not queued and a message says why.

Other engines: open **Infinite Movie - Engine LTX 2.5** or **Infinite Movie - Engine Wan 2.2**, copy its group (Ctrl+C), paste it here (Ctrl+V) and mute the MiniMax group (Ctrl+M) – only ONE engine group may be active.

## Required tools
- ffmpeg (encoding/joining films): usually already there via `imageio-ffmpeg` (installed with VideoHelperSuite), otherwise https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/ (Windows) or https://ffmpeg.org/download.html – put `ffmpeg` on PATH.
- VideoHelperSuite: https://github.com/Kosinkadink/ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite

## Models – MiniMax H3 (default engine)
- diffusion_models: [minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)
- loras: [minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.1_768p_comfyui_bf16](https://huggingface.co/lightx2v/Minimax-h3-Turbo/resolve/main/minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.1_768p_comfyui_bf16.safetensors)
- text_encoders (CLIPLoader type `minimax`): [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors)
- vae: [minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_int8_convrot.safetensors) · [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)
- Model page: https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3

## Optional
- LTX IC-LoRA pixel upscaler + https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo
- Low VRAM (12–16 GB, untested by us): community LTX-2.5 GGUF + https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF

**Tested on:** RTX 24 GB, 768×960, single shots up to 60 s (1441 frames).

nodes.title: Help: 2 · Images
widgets_values:
## 2 · Images
Your stills, top to bottom = order in the film.
- **Load Image** → Director `image 1`, `image 2`, …

nodes.title: Help: 3 · Prompts
widgets_values:
## 3 · Prompts
- **Prompt Style** (top): what the prompt model is told, `max_words`, `camera`. Applies to all Auto Prompts.
- **Auto Prompt** (one per transition, sits between its two images): type a few words into `keywords`, press **🔄 Regenerate prompt** – the model looks at both images and writes `prompt`. Edit it freely; Run never rewrites it.
- Output `prompt` → Director; `settings ▶ chain` → next node.

nodes.title: Help: 1 · Settings
widgets_values:
## 1 · Settings
One node for the whole workflow.
- `prompt_model`: local vision model that writes the prompts (Qwen3-VL in `models/text_encoders`); `off` = write them yourself.
- `aspect` + `long_side`: picture size (both sides rounded to 32; 4:5 + 960 = 768×960).
- `output_folder` (**📂 Choose folder**, default `infinite_movie` inside ComfyUI's output folder) and `film_name`: where the film goes and what it is called. Inside the folder: `cache_movies/<film_name>/` = the rendered shots (render cache, safe to delete), `raw/` = the chosen shots when `raw` is on.
- `raw`: also save the chosen shots one by one (`<film_name>_shot01.mp4` …, with sound) – for cutting them yourself.
- `audio`: sound from the engine (off = faster, silent film).
- **📦 Check models**: lists missing model files with their size and downloads them.
- Output `settings ▶ chain` → Prompt Style.

nodes.title: Help: 4 · Director
widgets_values:
## 4 · Director
Turns images + prompts into shots.
- `images`: number of images (adds or removes Load Image + Auto Prompt, then lays out; removed ones come back when raised).
- **Image list** (top = first): drag an image up or down – it gets a blue frame, a blue line between the images shows where it lands. ✕ removes it. Transitions with a new image pair get an empty prompt → 🔄 regenerate.
- `seconds` per shot, `loop` (last image back to the first), `variants` (2 = render A and B, pick in Cut), `seed`.
- **🔗 AUTO LAYOUT**: tidies all groups and wires Director → Cut → Even Motion.
- Output `sync ▶ Cut` → Cut: all shot data **and the settings** travel over this one link.

nodes.title: Help: 5 · Cut
widgets_values:
## 5 · Cut
Here the film is decided and made.
- Hover plays a shot; click picks it (A/B with `variants` = 2). **✓ KEEP / ✗ REDO** per shot; red *⚠ HARD CUT / SEAM* marks bad joins.
- **▶ play** under a shot shows it big with sound below; **▶ film** plays the finished film.
- **✎ prompt** / **⏱ seconds** change one shot and mark it REDO.
- Big button: **RENDER VIDEO ▶** joins the chosen shots into the film (with sound when Settings › `audio` is on) and runs everything behind Cut; **RERENDER n ↻** renders only the marked shots.
- Analysis of each shot: Heatmap · Frames · Particles · Sheet.
- Outputs `sync` → Even Motion (carries all shot data and the settings), `video_path` (the film) → Film / Upscale, `last_frame`, `first_frame`.

nodes.title: Help: 6 · Even Motion + Film
widgets_values:
## 6 · Even Motion + Film
- **Film**: plays the film from Cut, shows where it was saved, **📂 Open folder**.
- **Even Motion** (optional, off by default – select it, **Ctrl+M** turns it on): for smooth camera moves (architecture, fly-throughs). Re-picks the frames of every shot so each carries about the same change; `time_extend` (1–4×) makes the film longer and slower at the same fps from RIFE in-between frames. Writes `<film_name>_even.mp4` (silent). To watch or upscale it, connect its `video_path` to Film / Upscale instead of Cut's.
- Viewer: Graph · Timeline (grey = as rendered, coloured = evened out).

nodes.title: Help: 7 · Upscale
widgets_values:
## 7 · Upscale (optional)
- Off by default. **Select the group, Ctrl+M** turns it on.
- Then **RENDER VIDEO ▶** also renders an upscaled film with **RelayVSR x4**, scaled down to 1920 (calm and sharp), with the film's sound.
- **ram_gb** is the divider: the film is upscaled in segments that fit this much RAM – any length works. Lower it if RAM runs out.
- x2 is faster (relayvsr_x2_… + flash_vae_x2). Alternative: LTX Refine in `example_workflows/Upscaler/`.
- The second **Film** node shows the upscaled version.

nodes.title: Help: 0 · Engine: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## 0 · Engine (video model)
The engine renders one shot (start image → end image) per call from the Director. It is a normal, visible group:
**Engine Start** (from Director: images, prompt, seed, size, length) → *your model chain* → **Engine Result** (to Director: frames + sound).

| Engine | fps | Frames | Sound |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MiniMax H3** (this group, default) | 24 | 17k+5 | yes |
| LTX 2.5 | 24 | 8n+1 | yes |
| Wan 2.2 | 16 | 4n+1 | no |

**Switch engine:**
1. Templates (left bar) › *comfyui-infinite-movie* › open `Infinite Movie - Engine LTX 2.5` or `… Wan 2.2`.
2. Click its group title, **Ctrl+C**, come back here, **Ctrl+V**.
3. Mute this MiniMax group: click its title, **Ctrl+M**. Only **one** engine group may be active.
- **3 · 🔗 AUTO LAYOUT** on the Director – it finds the active Engine Result by itself.

**Own engine (any video model):** easiest is to copy an engine group and swap the model nodes. From scratch:
1. Double-click the canvas, add **Engine Start · Infinite Movie** and **Engine Result · Infinite Movie**.
2. Engine Start → your model: `start_image` / `end_image` → the image-to-video (first/last frame) node, `prompt` → text encoder, `seed` → sampler, `width` / `height` / `length` → the video/latent size.
3. Your decoded frames (IMAGE) → Engine Result › `images` (or a VIDEO → `video`), sound → `audio`.
4. Engine Result: `fps` = your model's fps, `length_grid` (advanced) = its frame step (Wan 4, LTX 8, H3 17).
5. Put it in a group, mute the other engine group (Ctrl+M), **🔗 AUTO LAYOUT**.
No hidden presets – what you see is what renders.

**This group (MiniMax H3):** first/last frame, int8, 8-step turbo LoRA v1.1 (768p). KSampler 8 steps, cfg 1, `res_multistep`, `simple`; negative = ConditioningZeroOut. Without the LoRA: bypass it, 20–25 steps. Sound is kept only when Settings › `audio` is on.

nodes.title: Story Mode (LLM) · how it works
widgets_values:
## Story Mode (LLM) · how it works
**▶ Switch it on:** this node comes **off** (purple = bypassed). Click it and press **Ctrl+B** – it turns grey like the others. Then do the **Setup** below. Ctrl+B again = off (the small `prompt_model` writes).

**Idea:** the small `prompt_model` sees only the two images of one shot. Story Mode lets a bigger vision LLM on a server read **all** images first and plan the film – an arc plus one beat per shot. widgets_values:
## 8 · Movie to GIF (optional)
- Off by default. **Select the node, Ctrl+M** turns it on; then **RENDER VIDEO ▶** also makes a GIF (or WebP / MP4 loop) of the film.
- Input: the film from Cut (`video_path`). Any video works: `video`, `images`, `video_path` or a file from the list.
- `format`, `long_side` (480 = small and sharp), `crop` (square, 4:5 …).
- Time, at the bottom above the preview: `start` / `end` cut a part, `direction` (forward, backward, ping-pong), **`speed`** changes the length (2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = slow motion), **`fps`** changes only the smoothness and the size (0 = the film's own rate).
- The preview line shows length, speed, fps and the expected file size before you save.
- **save** / **save as**; `auto_save (batch)` saves every run into `output_folder` (`filename` with # = counter).
